method.name: advance_frame
method.description: Advances the frame a received payload is stamped with while no clock is configured. It advances AFTER intake, so a payload read during a poll carries the frame it arrived in rather than the one after it.

method.name: carrier_append
method.description: Adds one frame to [param peer]'s run, sending whatever run it displaces. Answers the sequence that displaced datagram went out under, and [code]-1[/code] when nothing was displaced, when what went out was reliable, and when the send was refused. None of the three has a sequence to stage against.

method.name: carrier_clear
method.description: Drops every run still held without sending any of it.

method.name: carrier_flush
method.description: Sends every run still held, unreliable lane first. Answers the peer and the sequence of each unreliable datagram that went out, flat and in pairs, which is what a pass staged this tick has to be told before an acknowledgement for that sequence can promote anything.

method.name: carrier_pending
method.description: How many bytes of frames [param peer]'s run on the named lane is holding.

method.name: channel_aggregates
method.description: Whether a frame on [param channel] waits for a flush instead of leaving now. The channel declaration answers it, so the policy is one table rather than a list a sender and a declaration can come to disagree about. [param requested] is the sender's own ask, which the declaration may refuse.

method.name: count_sent
method.description: Counts one outbound packet and its [param bytes] together. A packet always carries its own byte count, so the pair advances in one verb. Two counters raised at four separate call sites drift the moment one of them forgets its second line.

method.name: count_standalone_ack_out
method.description: Counts one acknowledgement that had no datagram of its own to ride. It raises the outbound state-acknowledgement counter too, so the standalone count can never exceed it.

method.name: datagram_budget
method.description: How many bytes of frames one unreliable datagram may carry. The transport's own ceiling less the headroom the carrier header and the transport's command bytes take, floored so a pathologically small setting still admits one frame rather than refusing every send.

method.name: effect_arm
method.description: Arms the optimistic act [param key], parking [param revert] against a deadline. The deadline is the session's own tick plus [param timeout_ticks], so an act armed during a pump expires a whole wait later rather than at whatever tick a caller happened to read first. Zero takes the session default.

method.name: effect_watch
method.description: Watches the armed act [param key], answering [code]false[/code] when it is not armed. A watcher can therefore never outlive the act it observes.

method.name: entity_announce_reparented
method.description: The settled half of [method entity_settle_reparented], announcing [code]reparented[/code] on [param wrapper]. An owner that is gone or no longer in the tree is not reported at all, because the settle runs after the propagation and a report naming a node the listener cannot read is worse than none.

method.name: entity_at_or_above
method.description: The nearest handle at or above [param node], or an invalid [RID] when the walk finds none. The walk is over nodes because that is where the answer lives: an entity marks its root with [code]netw_entity[/code] metadata, so the nearest marked ancestor is the nearest entity.

method.name: entity_broadcast_control
method.description: Fans a settled controller to the peers that can see the entity. Off-session there is no plane to fan through, and that is the ordinary case rather than an error: every offline rig takes it on every transfer.

method.name: entity_describe
method.description: What this session holds about [param route], as one read a watcher can put beside an event record. [codeblock] { ┠╴route int the route asked about ┠╴entity_id StringName the durable label ┠╴peer_id int the peer this entity represents, 0 for a server-owned one ┠╴stage int a [enum NetwEntity.Stage] value ┠╴controller int the peer that steers it, 0 for the server ┠╴liveness int a [enum NetwLivenessCore.State] value ┖╴layers Array the interest layers it belongs to, in join order } [/codeblock] Empty for a route this session holds no record for. A lifecycle event names its subject and not its state, because attaching a projection to every event costs every session that emits one. This is the read that answers the state, and [constant DESPAWNED] carries the last one instead, since a route outlives its entity by exactly one event.

method.name: entity_derived_binding
method.description: The derived set binding of [param record] kind on [param owner], or [code]null[/code]. The owner's own marks win, then [param route]'s derived group answers a set a child node declares, such as an input mark living on a component under the root. Resolved per call, so a reparent is followed for free, matching how the retained lane and the pump re-resolve route per pass. A session told of no replication plane resolves nothing.

method.name: entity_derived_group
method.description: Every derived set binding declared on [param route], on any of its nodes.

method.name: entity_enter_tree
method.description: What a tree entry does to an entity: hydrate the identity, classify it, arm it, take a route, announce it, wire the node's own signals, and go live. A first entry classifies the record and goes live. A reparent re-entry keeps its live stage and only reapplies authority and scene registration for the new parent, so it is not a second birth. An entry the record classifies as inert, a template or a bare programmatic node, stops there. The order matters and is the whole reason this is one verb: identity, then control authority, then scene registration.

method.name: entity_free_owner
method.description: Frees [param owner]. The act a linger schedules, bound to the session rather than free-standing because a callable with no object reads as invalid and the settle queue skips those.

method.name: entity_governs_property
method.description: Whether a stream other than [param exclude] already drives the live target [param path] names under [param owner]. A persisted client-owned field that another stream drives is a double-authority mistake, and this is what flags it. [param exclude] exists because a stream is not competition with itself. Both halves are checked: every other [MultiplayerSynchronizer] on the owner, and every field a derived binding on [param route] declares.

method.name: entity_instantiate_copy
method.description: An unparented copy of [param template_node]'s scene, carrying NO marked spawn state, because the marks are resolved through a session or not at all. [param configure] runs on the copy's wrapper before the copy enters any tree.

method.name: entity_instantiate_from
method.description: An unparented copy of [param template_node]'s scene, carrying every marked value [method set_spawn_state_gather] names, resolved onto the copy's counterpart of each source node. A source the copy has no counterpart for is skipped rather than written onto the root. [param configure] runs on the copy's wrapper, which exists by then, because a caller configures the entity rather than the node.

method.name: entity_instantiate_player
method.description: An unparented copy of [param owner]'s scene bound to [param participant]'s identity. A participant that names no join has not been accepted, so it names no player to build one for and this answers [code]null[/code].

method.name: entity_linger
method.description: Deactivates [param owner] at once and frees it [param pumps] pumps later, which is what keeps a despawned target rewindable for a window a record plane with no tree counts as well as a rendered one does. The record and its owner are named by the caller rather than resolved from the session's index, because an entity is stamped with the session it belongs to before that session has adopted it.

method.name: entity_move
method.description: The node half of a reparent, which is all a record no session holds can have: the destination pose, the ready reset, and the move itself. [param record] carries the move as [member NetwEntityRecord.reparenting] for the duration, so an [code]_exit_tree[/code] consumer can tell a reparent from a despawn. An owner that no parent holds is added rather than moved, because [method Node.reparent] needs a parent to move away from.

method.name: entity_parent_of
method.description: The nearest ancestor handle of [param entity], or an invalid [RID] at a root. The walk is over nodes because that is where the answer lives: an entity marks its root, so the nearest marked ancestor is the nearest entity. It answers in handles because a caller asked about one.

method.name: entity_reparent
method.description: Moves [param owner] under [param new_parent], carrying its admission edge when [method entity_reparent_crosses] says the move leaves one scene for another. Admission moves BEFORE the reparent, so the destination's row is already flushed when the subtree's spawn packets go out. Membership itself needs no handoff: it is ancestry, and the new parent is the whole of it. A refused move leaves nothing in flight, because a record still holding one would read every later tree exit as a reparent and keep a dead route alive. The record and its owner are named by the caller for the same reason [method entity_linger]'s are.

method.name: entity_reparent_crosses
method.description: Whether moving [param entity] under [param destination] carries a player across a scene boundary, which is the only move that has to carry an admission edge as well as a parent. All three terms are needed: a server-owned entity is admitted nowhere, a destination under no declared scene has no boundary to admit to, and a destination inside the scene the player is already in re-sends an edge it already holds.

method.name: entity_request_control
method.description: Asks [param plane] to carry a control request for [param wrapper]. With no peer connected there is no server to route the ask to, so the request is decided where it was made instead of being dropped.

method.name: entity_scene_facet
method.description: The scene facet [param record]'s entity BELONGS to, which is its nearest declaring ancestor's, or its own when no scene resolves. Self-inclusive, so an entity that declares a scene answers itself. It resolves through [method entity_scene_of] rather than repeating the walk, so a caller asking which scene an entity is in and one asking which handle to announce cannot come to disagree. The record and its wrapper are named by the caller rather than resolved from the index, because an entity is asked which scene it is in before this session has adopted it, and one the index does not hold still belongs to a scene: its own.

method.name: entity_scene_of
method.description: The nearest handle at or above [param entity] whose record declares a scene, or an invalid [RID]. At-or-above, because a scene container is its own scene.

method.name: entity_settle_reparented
method.description: Reports a move at this session's next settle rather than inside the propagation that made it, because the subtree is still rebuilding there and every node is back in the tree by the settle. Unkeyed, because two moves in one cascade are two discontinuities and a consumer resetting its smoothing owes each of them an answer.

method.name: entity_spawn_copy_under
method.description: [method entity_spawn_under]'s seating over a copy carrying no marked spawn state, for a template no session holds.

method.name: entity_spawn_player
method.description: [method entity_instantiate_player]'s copy, handed to [param scene] as one of its players. A participant that builds no player is never seated.

method.name: entity_spawn_under
method.description: A copy of [param owner]'s scene, named after [param id] when one is given, seated under [param parent]. A [param parent] of [code]null[/code] seats the copy beside its template, and a template with neither seats nothing rather than leaking an unparented copy.

method.name: frame_datagram
method.description: The datagram [param payload] rides to [param peer], stamped and booked. One call, because the stamp, the echo it piggybacks, and the record that this peer is no longer owed a standalone acknowledgement are one decision. Split apart, a caller could frame under a sequence it had not asked for yet.

method.name: get_inner
method.description: The transport this carrier writes through. A [SceneMultiplayer] rather than the [MultiplayerPeer] under it, because [method SceneMultiplayer.send_bytes] is not a thin wrapper: it prepends the raw command byte the receiving side demuxes on, relays a client-to-client datagram through the server, honours a negative target as broadcast-with-exclusion, and refuses a peer that is not connected.

method.name: get_local_player
method.description: The wrapper this peer is represented by, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: handle_of_wrapper
method.description: The handle [param wrapper] carries, or an invalid [RID] for a wrapper this session never adopted, which is what separates another session's entity from one of ours.

method.name: has_wrapper_factory
method.description: Returns whether anything has registered how to build an entity wrapper.

method.name: interest_sync_record
method.description: Writes one entity's place in the interest engine: its parent link and its deterministic (depth, route) order. Ancestors are written first, because a clamp that read a parent the engine has not heard of would leave the child unspawnable until something else happened to touch the parent. The chain climbs from each entity's owner to the nearest record above it, and stops at a key it has already seen, so a parent link that closes on itself costs one pass rather than the process. An entity with no route of its own is ordered by [method NetwInterestEngine.order_route_for], since the route tiebreak has to be total before there is a route.

method.name: liveness_adopt
method.description: Introduces [param wrapper] to this session, so the index answers for it, and hands back the handle it already carries. Idempotent, and it never mints: the handle is the wrapper's own, held since it was constructed.

method.name: liveness_adopt_route
method.description: Gives [param route] to [param wrapper], adopting the record the route already stands for when it stands for a dead one. A route names one entity across every life it has, so a re-admission takes the standing handle rather than minting a second name for it, and the record comes back live one epoch higher. Answers [constant @GlobalScope.OK] when the caller now owes the announcement, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS] when [param wrapper] was already standing on a live route and owes nothing, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] when the route belongs to another entity or already carries an identity this session holds. The announcement is [method liveness_publish_live], separately, because the caller wires the wrapper's own node signals in between and a listener must not learn the route is live before those are standing.

method.name: liveness_allocate_route
method.description: The route [param wrapper] stands on, reserving and binding one when it stands on none. Two asks about one entity answer the same route.

method.name: liveness_bind
method.description: Binds [param wrapper] to [param route] in the record plane and the index at once. Answers [code]false[/code] when the plane refused, and changes nothing when it does, so a caller never wires a route the plane does not hold. Announcing is [method liveness_publish_live], separately, because the caller wires the wrapper's own node signals in between and a listener must not learn the route is live before those are standing.

method.name: liveness_bind_route
method.description: Gives [param route] to [param wrapper] and announces it live, reading the wrapper's own [NetwEntityRecord] and owner rather than being handed them. The order inside is the contract: the owner's [signal Node.tree_exiting] and the wrapper's despawn hook stand BEFORE [method liveness_publish_live], because a listener must not learn a route is live while the signals that will retire it are unconnected.

method.name: liveness_bind_routes_data
method.description: Binds every route in [param routes] as a live entity with no wrapper and no node, which is the identity a replicated table row is. It emits no [signal entity_live], because a wave of two thousand rows carries no wrapper a listener could reach through. A caller parked on [method NetwMultiplayer.when_live] is still answered.

method.name: liveness_clear_session
method.description: Empties the record plane and the wrapper index between sessions. Wrappers keep their handles, which outlive every session that adopts one.

method.name: liveness_linger
method.description: Moves [param entity] to [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING] and emits [signal entity_lingering].

method.name: liveness_live_entities
method.description: Every wrapper this peer currently holds a [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LIVE] route for, ordered by route so two calls in one frame agree. This is the peer's own visible set and nothing more: a route is here only because this peer was sent the spawn.

method.name: liveness_node_of
method.description: The root [Node] [param route] names, or [code]null[/code] once the tree has freed it.

method.name: liveness_owner_despawning
method.description: Moves a lingering teardown's route to [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING]. A despawn without linger changes nothing here, because its route dies at the owner's tree exit instead.

method.name: liveness_owner_exiting
method.description: Resolves an owner leaving the tree. A move in flight is not a teardown, so a [member NetwEntity.reparenting] entity is left alone. A route the spawn ledger tracks resolves at the next settle through [method liveness_resolve_tracked_exit] instead, so a remove-then-add reparent before that pump never kills the route.

method.name: liveness_pending_live_count
method.description: How many parked callbacks are still waiting for a binding, the liveness backlog [InterestMonitor] surfaces.

method.name: liveness_poll
method.description: Advances the record plane's frame counter and expires whatever aged out, warning for each route whose last waiter timed out. Pass the tick a configured clock reads, or [code]0[/code] when none is.

method.name: liveness_publish_live
method.description: Announces [param route] live as [signal entity_live], resolving the wrapper from the index itself. It takes only the route, because the session is what knows which wrapper that route names and a caller passing one could pass a different one than the index holds.

method.name: liveness_reserve_route
method.description: Advances the route counter and answers what it handed out, binding nothing to it. Allocation is monotonic and a route is never reused, tombstone included, so a name this returns can only ever mean the entity that claims it.

method.name: liveness_resolve_tracked_exit
method.description: The settled half of the reparent grace: a tracked owner back inside the tree was reparented, and anything else is a real despawn. A [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING] route resolves here too, so a linger-then-free still reaches [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_DEAD].

method.name: liveness_retire
method.description: Retires [param route]: the state move to [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_DEAD], the waiter drop, the index move from live to retired, and [signal entity_dead]. One act, because the announcement carries a route whose wrapper a listener must be able to resolve exactly as it will be for the rest of the cycle. It clears [member local_player] only when the entity DYING is the one representing this peer, asked by identity rather than by route: a scene change binds the replacement before retiring the original, so a route-keyed test drops a local player that had already moved on.

method.name: liveness_route_of
method.description: The route bound to [param wrapper], or [code]0[/code].

method.name: liveness_route_state
method.description: The [enum NetwLivenessCore.State] of [param route].

method.name: liveness_settle_local_player
method.description: Settles which entity represents this peer, now that [param route] is live. Separate from [method liveness_publish_live] because a listener on the live edge reads [member local_player] while the cascade runs, so the answer changes at the point in that cascade where it always has. It takes only the route and reads the entity's own [NetwEntityRecord], so a caller cannot name a local player the session did not choose. A session with no transport represents nobody.

method.name: liveness_state_of
method.description: The [enum NetwLivenessCore.State] of [param wrapper], or [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_UNKNOWN] for a wrapper carrying no record.

method.name: liveness_tombstone_routes_data
method.description: Tombstones every route in [param routes] without emitting [signal entity_dead], the death edge of [method liveness_bind_routes_data]. A tombstoned route is never reissued, which is what lets a receiver drop a row for it rather than resurrect one.

method.name: liveness_transition_dead
method.description: Retires [param route] with its wrapper's node and despawn hooks taken down first, so the retirement announcement cannot reach the handler that caused it.

method.name: liveness_when_live
method.description: Parks [param callback] on [param route] until it goes live, running it at once when the route already is. [param deadline] is a plain integer and [param on_clock] names which counter it is measured against, because the tick clock is a session service a rig may never configure. [method NetwMultiplayer.when_live] is the door that settles both from a timeout in ticks.

method.name: participant_adopt
method.description: Adopts [param participant] as [param peer]'s roster row. A peer already holding one keeps it, so two asks answer the same object rather than two. The row is minted by the caller and held here, for the same reason the wrapper index holds a reference: this is what keeps it alive.

method.name: participant_all
method.description: Every roster row, un-joined observers included, in peer order so two reads in one frame agree.

method.name: participant_clear
method.description: Drops every row. Session teardown, so a same-session re-host starts empty.

method.name: participant_forget
method.description: Drops [param peer]'s row.

method.name: participant_has
method.description: Whether [param peer] holds a row.

method.name: participant_of
method.description: [param peer]'s roster row, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: participant_publish_joined
method.description: Announces [param peer]'s row as joined, and binds it as the local participant when that peer is this one, before the announcement, so a listener that reacts by changing scene has its change published rather than dropped. It takes only the peer, because the session holds the row and decides for itself whether that peer is this one: the local announcement has to precede the general one, and a caller deciding which to send could send them in either order or send only one.

method.name: poll_delta
method.description: Seconds since the previous poll, and zero on a session's first poll because there is no earlier one to measure against. Reading it MARKS this poll, so a second reader in the same frame is answered zero. [param now_usec] is the caller's reading of the wall clock, handed down rather than taken here.

method.name: property_path
method.description: [param property] on [param source], relative to [param base]. Empty when either node is gone, because falling through would answer a bare property name that writes whichever node the reader happened to hold. A node addresses itself as [code]"."[/code], so a property on the base is a valid self-address.

method.name: receive_header
method.description: Reads one inbound datagram's header, announcing and counting as it goes. A packet that is not Networked framing is emitted as [signal peer_packet] rather than answered about, because the session is the only thing that can tell the application's traffic from its own. Everything the session does own is counted into [member received_packets] and [member received_bytes], body bytes only, so two peers' throughput is comparable. A datagram of ours that cannot be read is neither announced nor counted. It answers the header rather than only the kind so a caller drives the rest from one read. The read is a three-way answer, and a watched session sees all three ways it can go: a datagram of ours leaves a [code]DATAGRAM_RECEIVED[/code] row, one of ours that cannot be read leaves a [code]DATAGRAM_MALFORMED[/code] row, and the application's own traffic leaves neither because it was never ours to report.

method.name: relative_path
method.description: A path from [param source] to [param target], empty when either is gone. The one spelling, so a path built for a wire address and one built for a property binding cannot come to differ.

method.name: scene_build_container
method.description: The orphan container one scene mounts under, built for the isolation it declared. A hosting peer isolates an [param own_world] scene in a [SubViewport] with its own 3D world and no render target, and every other case is a plain [Node], because only the host simulates. Neither carries a script: a scene is its entity record, not a node class. The container is named [code]Scene[/code] and carries [method scene_container_meta], so a walk with no session to ask can still find one. The caller owns it and parents it.

method.name: scene_container_meta
method.description: The metadata key [method scene_build_container] stamps a container with. One spelling, read from here rather than written a second time, because the walk that reads it runs off-session where nothing else identifies a container.

method.name: scene_handle_of
method.description: The scene facet [param entity] publishes itself through, or [code]null[/code] for an entity this session holds no record for. It is the record's own facet ([constant NetwEntityRecord.PART_SCENE]) rather than a copy the session was handed, because the handle IS the scene's public identity and two would be two scenes.

method.name: scene_install_level
method.description: Mounts [param level] as [param container]'s only child and renames the container after it, which is what makes a container's first child its content root. Either being gone installs nothing rather than half-mounting.

method.name: scene_layer_id
method.description: The layer id naming [param scene]'s admission boundary, or empty when its container holds no content root. It is the content root's name and, once the scene has one, its route, because a stem alone collides across two live scenes built from the same content. A scene armed this frame has no route yet and is keyed by the stem alone until one lands. Distinct from [method scene_stem], which prefers a declared label. A caller asking what a scene is CALLED and a caller asking which layer admits it are not asking the same question.

method.name: scene_packed_stem
method.description: The stem [param packed] would enter the live book under, which is the name of its content root. Empty for a null or contentless scene. It is deliberately NOT the resource path's file name. A scene file is named in snake_case and its root node in PascalCase by convention, so the two disagree for almost every scene, and a lookup keyed on the file name finds nothing and silently spawns a duplicate.

method.name: scene_publish_live
method.description: Records the scene [param route] names as live under [param name] and announces [param container]'s handle as [signal scene_live], in one act: two adjacent calls are two chances to send one without the other. The container is named by the caller rather than walked to here, because [method entity_scene_of] is one stage of a resolution the caller owns, and a second walk would be a second answer. The handle it announces is [method scene_handle_of] on the key you name here, so the announcement cannot publish a handle nobody holds.

method.name: scene_request_flooded
method.description: Whether [param peer]'s scene requests have passed the rate the session admits joins under, counting one [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_BUSY] verdict when they have. The host carries authority and is never limited. [param now_msec] is handed in rather than read, so the window is a function of its arguments and a case can drive it without a clock.

method.name: scene_stem
method.description: The non-unique stem [param scene] answers to: the label a script declared through [member NetwEntity.scene_label], and otherwise the content root's name. Empty for a scene no record stands for. One answer rather than two, because the content root's name is the key the live book files a scene under, so a caller that read the two separately would be comparing one fact spelled twice.

method.name: schema_create
method.description: The handle for the schema named [param name], minting one when this session holds none. Declaring a name that already exists answers the handle it already has and restarts that schema's re-declaration cursor, so a script reload replays its own columns rather than minting a second schema.

method.name: schema_find
method.description: The handle this session holds for [param name], or an invalid [RID] when it holds none. The lookup alone. Compiling a declaration this session has not adopted stays above the core, because a registry of declarations is GDScript and a core that read one would be reaching back across the seam it defines.

method.name: send_datagram
method.description: Frames one datagram and hands it to the transport. Answers the sequence it went out under, or [code]-1[/code] for a reliable datagram and for a refusal. A refusal is a datagram that was never sent, so the two share an answer here only because neither has a sequence to report.

method.name: service_all
method.description: Every service whose script is [param base] or derives from it, in registration order.

method.name: service_clear
method.description: Drops every registered service. Silent, because a session that is ending announces its own end and a per-service notice would repeat what every listener has already been told.

method.name: service_of
method.description: The service registered under [param type], or [code]null[/code]. A service the game freed reads as absent, because the book holds an id rather than a reference: keeping one would outlive the scene that made it.

method.name: service_register
method.description: Registers [param service] under [param type], defaulting to its own script, and emits [signal service_registered]. Re-registering the identical instance is inert, because a service that auto-registers on entering the tree may also be registered explicitly.

method.name: service_unregister
method.description: The twin of [method service_register], honoured only while [param type] still names [param service].

method.name: session_publish_control
method.description: Announces the session control frame [param channel] carries, and answers whether it was consumed here. The channel decides which announcement it is, the authority rule decides whether this session honours it at all, and the payload decodes the same way for every one of them; those three are one decision, so a caller routes a frame here rather than keeping a copy of the mapping. Consumed and refused are the same answer, [code]true[/code]: the channel was this band's, so a caller must not fall through and route it elsewhere. A channel outside the band answers [code]false[/code].

method.name: set_replication_plane
method.description: Where the replication plane lives while it is still script-owned. The session is told once rather than reached through the shell, so a native verb that needs it asks the session and not its GDScript twin.

method.name: set_spawn_state_gather
method.description: Registers how this session answers "which marked properties ride a spawn". [param gather] takes the template node and answers an [Array] of [code]{node, prop}[/code] rows in the order the receiver applies them. The declaration registry is script-owned, so the session is told once rather than reaching into it per instantiation. A session told nothing carries nothing.

method.name: set_wrapper_factory
method.description: Registers how to build an entity wrapper. [param factory] takes the root node and answers the wrapper, already attached to it. Process-wide and outliving every session, because an entity is constructed, configured and read before any session exists, exactly as [NetwEntityIds] is. The extension drops the factory at shutdown.

method.name: settle_advance
method.description: Spends one pump against every window [method settle_schedule_after] is holding. Separate from the drain, because a clocked session drains on its polls as well as its ticks and a window is counted in the cadence the session sends at. Calling it twice a pump spends the window twice.

method.name: settle_schedule_after
method.description: Holds [param fn] for [param pumps] pumps before a settle will run it. A window counted in the session's own pumps needs no [SceneTree] and no wall clock, so a teardown that has to stay reachable for a while is expressible where a scene tree is not. [param key] coalesces exactly as it does for [method settle_schedule], so re-declaring a window replaces it rather than queuing a second one. A window still open is not a settle that failed to reach a fixed point, so it is never reported as one.

method.name: sink_verdict
method.description: Counts one remote-input [param verdict] on [param route], says whatever it is worth saying, and answers the verdict. The three things a verdict is worth are one partition rather than three call sites. A route this peer has not seen, one that is dead and one whose node is gone are ordinary traffic and stay silent. [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED], [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_BUSY] name a sender that sent what it may not, and warn once per verdict and route together, so one peer retrying cannot flood a log. Anything outside the partition is this session's own defect and is reported as an error, because a sink that answered something which is not a verdict has a bug rather than a new row. [constant @GlobalScope.OK] is not a verdict. It counts nothing and reports nothing, which is why a gate that admitted a frame is visible through [method gate_verdict] and not here.

method.name: stage_verdict
method.description: Records that [param stage] ran on [param route] and answered [param verdict], and answers the verdict back, so a caller reads the stage and its answer as one expression. [param stage] is a gate ([constant GATE_SYNC], [constant GATE_SPAWN], [constant GATE_TABLE], [constant GATE_PREDICT]) or a pipeline stage ([constant SPAWN_DECLARE], [constant SPAWN_RECONCILE] and the rest of that range). A watched session gets one row of that kind for every run, including the ones that answered [constant @GlobalScope.OK], because "this stage ran and admitted it" is the fact an observer most often wants and the one a verdict count cannot carry. Everything else the verdict is worth is [method sink_verdict]'s, so a stage cannot count its answer one way and report it another.

method.name: spawn_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound spawn, despawn or reparent frame, and the body an override of the spawn admission seam narrows rather than replaces. Materialization is server-authored, so [param sender] is judged before anything else: a peer other than the server is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] whatever channel it named. A channel outside the three this gate admits, or an empty [param payload], is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA]. [param route] is unresolved by construction, because the frame that creates a route arrives before that route exists. It travels so an override can read it.

method.name: table_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound table frame, and the body an override of the table admission seam narrows rather than replaces. It takes no route because a table frame is route-0 addressed and the routes it carries are knowable only mid-decode, so everything it judges is in the header: who sent it, which table it names, and whether that table's sealed schema agrees. A frame from a peer other than the server is counted on [member table_core] as well as refused, because the count is what separates a rejected sender from a table nobody is publishing.

method.name: table_commit
method.description: Fixes [param table]'s written routes and columns as the applied state readers compare against. Stamped with the session's own tick, because a commit is what fixes the frame a reader dates itself against and two clocks would date it twice.

method.name: table_create
method.description: A table over [param schema], keyed by the schema's name. Binding a schema whose name already carries a table answers that table, so a script reload finds its own handle rather than minting a second one. An unsealed schema has no address order yet and is refused.

method.name: table_publish
method.description: Announces one table as [signal table_received], stamped with the tick its commit fixed. For the send side, where a commit made this tick is announced beside the ones an intake produced.

method.name: table_publish_intake
method.description: Announces every table this tick's intake touched, then opens the next intake window. The two are one act: announcing without reopening announces the same tables again next tick, and reopening without announcing loses the wave. The set is [member table_core]'s own, so a table the decoder never wrote to is never named.

method.name: wrapper_adopt
method.description: Introduces [param wrapper] to this session under [param entity], so the index answers for it. Idempotent, and it never mints. [b]This index is the one place an entity wrapper is held.[/b] A wrapper is reference counted and nothing else keeps it alive, so the index holds a reference rather than an id: an id-only index frees the wrapper the moment the caller that made it lets go, and every later resolve answers a dead object.

method.name: wrapper_at
method.description: The wrapper at or above [param node], read from [method wrapper_meta] metadata, or [code]null[/code] when the walk finds none. An unmarked node in between is not an entity, so the walk passes through it rather than stopping.

method.name: wrapper_bind
method.description: Names [param node] after the identity and stamps it onto the node's wrapper, minting one through [method set_wrapper_factory] when the node carries none. An [param entity_id] the codec cannot name binds NOTHING, because a name that spells no identity would leave the node and the record disagreeing about who the entity is.

method.name: wrapper_clear
method.description: Drops both sides of the index. Session teardown.

method.name: wrapper_ensure
method.description: The wrapper on [param root] itself, minted through [method set_wrapper_factory] when it carries none. A node is given one wrapper and keeps it, so two callers asking answer the same object.

method.name: wrapper_for_id
method.description: Live or retired, which is the door an engine resolves a delta row through: a removed entity's last act is a hide to every peer that held it, and the transition naming it arrives in the NEXT delta.

method.name: wrapper_for_route
method.description: The route-keyed twin of [method wrapper_of].

method.name: wrapper_live
method.description: Every wrapper this peer holds a live route for, ordered by route so two calls in one frame agree.

method.name: wrapper_meta
method.description: The metadata an entity root carries its wrapper in. One spelling, shared by the wrapper that writes it and every walk that reads it.

method.name: wrapper_of
method.description: The live wrapper carrying [param entity], or [code]null[/code]. A wrapper a death retired is not live and answers [code]null[/code] here; [method wrapper_for_id] still finds it.

method.name: wrapper_owner
method.description: The root node [param entity] names, or [code]null[/code] once the tree has freed it. Held by id rather than by reference, because the tree owns it.

method.name: wrapper_resolve
method.description: The wrapper for [param node], provisioned on the topmost orphan above it when nothing in the chain carries one. A record provisioned on the leaf would name a node that is about to become somebody else's child. Answers [code]null[/code] once the tree holds [param node] or any of its ancestors, because that is past the moment a record could be provisioned. Use [method wrapper_ensure] to force one onto an exact node.

method.name: wrapper_sweep_retired
method.description: Drops every wrapper a death retired, one full cycle after the retirement, which is the moment the index's last grip on it goes.

members.member: Which handler answers for each wire channel, on both the entity lane and the peer-scoped one. It is the session's rather than any one interface's, because a registration has to outlive the interface that made it: every core writes its own rows here at construction and the replication interface dissolves before they do.

Whether this peer holds server authority, as either a dedicated or a listen server. Distinct from [member is_server], which answers peer IDENTITY: a peer can carry unique id 1 before the session machine has resolved any role at all.

The entity this peer is represented by, or [code]null[/code] when none represents it. The handle is kept beside the wrapper rather than looked up by route, because a retirement has to ask whether the DYING entity is the one representing this peer, and asking that by route answers yes for every entity that has one. A scene change spawns the replacement before retiring the original, so a route-keyed test drops a local player that had already moved on.

What the display plane holds for each entity, addressed by the entity's [RID] or by its route. On the session plane rather than on the display core, so a read that only needs a row does not need the core.

signal.name: after_tick
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.after_tick] from [member clock_core] under the session's own name, so a consumer holding the session never has to hold the clock.

signal.name: after_tick_loop
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.after_tick_loop] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.before_tick] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: before_tick_loop
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.before_tick_loop] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: clock_synchronized
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.clock_synchronized] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: disconnect_requested
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when a client asks to leave. Heard only by a session holding peer id 1, and [param peer_id] is the frame's sender rather than anything the payload claims.

signal.name: display_offset_insufficient
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.display_offset_insufficient] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: entity_dead
signal.description: Emitted by [method liveness_retire]. The wrapper has already left the live index for the retired one by the time this fires, so a listener resolving it through [method wrapper_for_id] reads the same answer it will read for the rest of the cycle.

signal.name: entity_lingering
signal.description: Emitted by [method liveness_linger]. The wrapper stays live in the index, because a lingering entity is still resolvable.

signal.name: entity_live
signal.description: Emitted by [method liveness_publish_live], carrying the wrapper the index holds rather than one a caller passed alongside, so a listener resolves the same object the session will answer with for the rest of the route's life.

signal.name: kick_requested
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when a client asks for a peer to be kicked. Heard only by a session holding peer id 1. A payload that is not the target-and-reason pair names no target and is dropped rather than announced against a default one.

signal.name: kicked
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when server authority kicks this peer, before the transport closes. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: local_participant_joined
signal.description: Emitted by [method participant_publish_joined] when the joining peer is this one, ahead of [signal participant_joined], so a listener handling both sees itself arrive before it sees the roster grow.

signal.name: local_scene_changed
signal.description: Republishes the scene change of the participant this session decided is the local peer, bound when that row joins and released when the roster drops it. Another peer changing scene is not this session changing scene.

signal.name: local_player_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the entity representing this peer changes, including to [code]null[/code] when the route carrying it retires. Decided where a route goes live, because that is the only moment the answer can change, and read off the entity's own [NetwEntityRecord] rather than through the wrapper. A session with no transport represents nobody, which an offline session answering unique id 1 would otherwise look like.

signal.name: on_tick
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.on_tick] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: participant_joined
signal.description: Emitted by [method participant_publish_joined] for every admitted peer, this one included. A peer with no roster row has not been admitted and is never announced.

signal.name: peer_authenticating
signal.description: Republishes [signal SceneMultiplayer.peer_authenticating] from the transport this session holds. A transport the session replaces stops republishing at once.

signal.name: peer_authentication_failed
signal.description: Republishes [signal SceneMultiplayer.peer_authentication_failed] from the transport this session holds, after recording the refusal as a [code]PEER_AUTH_FAILED[/code] event, so a sink reads it in the order the session decided it.

signal.name: peer_packet
signal.description: Emitted by [method receive_header] for a datagram that is not Networked framing, so the application's own byte traffic reaches it over the same transport. A datagram that IS ours and is unreadable is never announced here.

signal.name: server_disconnecting
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when the server announces it is going away. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: scene_live
signal.description: Emitted by [method scene_publish_live] for the scene a newly live route belongs to. The handle is the one adopted for the container the publisher named, so a node inside a scene announces the scene and not itself.

signal.name: service_registered
signal.description: Emitted by [method service_register]. Announcing is part of registering rather than something a caller adds, so every door announces: the flat verb on the session and the registry's own both arrive at the same place. Re-registering the identical instance is inert and announces nothing.

signal.name: service_unregistered
signal.description: Emitted by [method service_unregister], and only when the type still names that service, so a service already replaced cannot unregister the one that replaced it.

signal.name: session_ended
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwSessionCore.session_ended] from [member session_core]. It rides the departure from [constant NetwSessionCore.STATE_ONLINE], so a bring-up that failed before reaching it never announces an ending.

signal.name: session_entered
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwSessionCore.session_entered] from [member session_core]. It rides the arrival at [constant NetwSessionCore.STATE_ONLINE].

signal.name: poll_started
signal.description: Emitted by [method poll_delta], because marking a poll is what a poll starting is. [param delta] is the wall-clock gap since the previous mark, and zero on the session's first. A second reader in the same moment marked nothing and is announced nothing.

signal.name: stability_changed
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwClockCore.stability_changed] from [member clock_core].

signal.name: state_changed
signal.description: Republishes [signal NetwSessionCore.state_changed] from [member session_core]. An edge the machine refuses is not a transition, so it is not published.

signal.name: table_received
signal.description: Emitted by [method table_publish] and [method table_publish_intake] for one table an intake touched or a commit produced. [param tick] is the one the commit stamped, so several commits inside one tick collapse to the last.

signal.name: tree_paused
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when server authority pauses the session. Pausing the engine is a subscriber's reaction rather than part of the decision, so the session announces the edge once and everything that reacts reads the same announcement. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: tree_unpaused
signal.description: The twin of [signal tree_paused].
